{"body":"**PRD ID:** F13\n### Summary\nOne tap saves every received photo.\n### Acceptance (Given / When / Then)\nGiven 12 received photos on a phone, when \"Save all\" is tapped, then the share sheet opens once with all 12. On a laptop they download. Edge: real-device check on iPhone and Android stays unticked for the user.\n\n\n### Decisions (owner, 23 Nov, answering Codebase Wisdom's questions)\n- **The share sheet can't take the whole batch** (`navigator.canShare({ files })` is false: too many, too large or a type it won't take): **download them all**, one download per file, videos included.\n- **Which photos:** only fully received ones (a verified file in `files`, not this device's own). Photos still arriving are skipped, and Save all says how many, for example \"Saved 10 · 2 still arriving\". \"Still arriving\" counts only full-photo transfers already on their way to this device (not thumbnails, and not other devices' prints that were never dragged here: those aren't mentioned).\n- **Cancel or failure:** a cancelled share sheet (`AbortError`) does nothing. Any other failure (for example `NotAllowedError` when the tap no longer counts) doesn't start downloads by itself: a toast says \"Couldn't open the share sheet. Tap Save all again to download\", and the next tap downloads them all.\n\n\n- **When the message shows:** only after the share sheet reports success. It says \"Shared 10 · 2 still arriving\", not \"Saved\" (the sheet finishing only means the photos went somewhere: Save Image, AirDrop…). After a cancel, nothing is shown, and the photos stay available.\n- **After the share sheet fails:** the next tap downloads everything not yet handed over: the failed batch plus anything that finished arriving since. A per-photo \"handed over\" flag (set when it was shared or downloaded) means nothing is downloaded twice and nothing is missed. Download mode ends after one download batch: the tap after that tries the share sheet again.\n- **Downloads:** one at a time, about 300–500 ms apart (browsers block or prompt on a burst). No zip. The message says \"Downloading 10\", not \"Saved 10\": the page can't confirm what the browser kept.\n","title":"F13 · Save all"}
# Scenario format for group-device-check

A JSON file:

```json
{
  "ticket": 12,
  "devices": [{ "size": "laptop" }, { "size": "phone" }, { "size": "tablet" }],
  "steps": [ ... ]
}
```

- `devices`: 2–20 of `laptop` (900×600), `phone` (390×700), `tablet` (768×1000). They're joined in order (0–1, 1–2 …). Device 0 is usually the sender.
  - `"share": "fail-once"`: a stand-in share sheet that rejects its first call with `NotAllowedError`, then works.
  - `"share": "works"`: one that always works.
  - Without `share`, the device has no share sheet, as on a laptop.
- `steps` run in order. Actions:
  - `{"do":"pick","device":0,"count":3}`: draw and pick that many numbered photos (`1.jpg` … continuing across picks) on that device.
  - `{"do":"drag","from":0,"to":1,"photo":"2.jpg"}`: drag a print that is on device `from`'s screen onto device `to`'s screen. A print already moved to another screen can't be dragged from the first one again.
  - `{"do":"wait","device":1,"files":3}`: wait until that device holds that many full files and nothing is still arriving.
  - `{"do":"tap","device":1,"selector":"#saveall"}`: click an element.
  - `{"do":"pause","ms":1000}`.
- Checks: each needs `"source"`, the ticket section its expected value is copied from (never a code path).
  - `{"check":"toast","device":1,"equals":"…","source":"#12 Acceptance"}`: the message shown. Exact text, except curly and straight quotes count as equal.
  - `{"check":"downloads","device":1,"count":3,"source":"…"}`: how many downloads since the last tap on that device, each byte-identical to what the sender holds.
  - `{"check":"shared","device":1,"calls":1,"files":3,"source":"…"}`: on a stand-in share sheet, the number of calls so far and the number of files in the last one.

## Example (a different, made-up ticket: "a tapped print says Receiving… once")

```json
{
  "ticket": 12,
  "devices": [{ "size": "laptop" }, { "size": "phone" }],
  "steps": [
    { "do": "pick", "device": 0, "count": 1 },
    { "do": "drag", "from": 0, "to": 1, "photo": "1.jpg" },
    { "check": "toast", "device": 1, "equals": "Receiving…", "source": "#12 Acceptance: the receiver sees Receiving… while it arrives" }
  ]
}
```

Devices: 0 laptop (sender, no share sheet), 1 phone (stand-in share sheet, `fail-once`), 2 tablet (stand-in share sheet, `works`).
Scenario: `scenario.json` (11 check points, every expected value from #72 Acceptance or Decisions).

| Build | Commit | Verdict | First failing or stopping check (expected vs actual) | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PR #130 | 18ba6fb | PASS | none (11/11) | `pr130-18ba6fb/` |
| PR #135 | bc2de62 | FAIL | step 13, phone, #72 Decisions: Downloads: expected "Downloading 3", actual "Saved 3" (also step 24, laptop: "Downloading 1" vs "Saved 1") | `pr135-bc2de62/` |
| PR #140 | 585b85a | PASS | none (11/11) | `pr140-585b85a/` |

Stand-in share sheet: the phone and tablet windows used it (headless Chromium has none). It shows the app's logic, not a real phone. The laptop had none.

Notes:
- The PR #135 screenshots for steps 13 and 24 show no toast: the toast had gone by the time the screenshot was taken (the check waits 4 s for the expected text). The failure comes from the toast text read in `facts.json`, not from the image.
- Not exercised: a cancelled share sheet (`AbortError`, the stand-in has no cancel mode), "· N still arriving" (the scenario can't hold a transfer in flight), and the tap after a download batch trying the share sheet again (the ticket doesn't say how many files that share should carry).
